interface.title: fraud_screen: Research Source Data Numerical Anomaly Screening Demo (V1.2.0-beta)
interface.field: Research integrity / scientific publishing (biomedical source data review)
interface.stage_of_work: Post-publication or peer review: first screening of a paper's numbers before a person reviews it
interface.what_it_is_for: Upload a paper's Source Data tables, run numerical anomaly detectors (duplicate vectors, constant offsets/linear relations, SEM/SD/n consistency, digit patterns, smoothness), and get a risk score, a manual-review priority queue and downloadable reports.

data.note: I used example_fabricated.csv (1.4 KB, 1 sheet, 23 records, figures fig1/fig2/fig3) through the uploader, and also ran the built-in synthetic demo (paper 'synth_demo', no upload). Example file result: risk score 390, 16 flags (High/Med/Low 4/12/0, P1/P2/P3 3/13/0). Built-in demo result: risk score 150, 6 flags.

tree.general: Screen a paper's published numerical data for anomaly patterns and pass a ranked list of suspicious items to a human reviewer
tree.specific: Upload Source Data CSV/Excel to fraud_screen, run the detectors, read the risk summary and Top 20 Manual Review Items, and download the HTML/JSON/CSV/ZIP reports

features.name: Risk summary card with level legend
features.general: Sum up many detector hits as one score plus counts by severity and priority, with a legend that maps score ranges to levels
features.specific: Risk Score, Anomaly Flags, High/Med/Low, P1/P2/P3 metrics, 'Level: very high anomaly signal', an overall-verdict banner, and a Risk level explanation expander (Level 0 <10 ... Level 4 ≥70)
steps: Run a screening
Read the score and counts
Expand Risk level explanation to see the level bands
Use the P1/P2/P3 counts to plan the review effort

features.name: Prioritised manual-review queue table
features.general: A ranked table of flagged items, each with priority, confidence, which check fired, points, location, evidence and a suggested follow-up action, which the reviewer can sort, search, trim to the columns they need and open full screen
features.specific: Top 20 Manual Review Items data grid (P, C, Detector, Pts, Figure, Evidence, Action) with column-header sort, Search (match count and highlights), Show/hide columns and Fullscreen in its toolbar. Sort order and hidden columns reset on the next run. The toolbar also has Download as CSV, which gave no file in this run; the queue is exported with DL Review Queue instead.

screens_never_reached: An on-page target-figure review panel: target and case review results only came as downloads, and no section for them appeared on the page
DL Quality Report and DL Performance Log stayed '(not generated)' in every run I made; I did not find which setting turns them on
source_data_inventory.csv as its own download: it is named in the sidebar and the manifest but has no button (it may be inside the ZIP, which I could not open)
A 'matched' target state: every target came back not_found
An error or warning screen: none appeared for a missing config path or for Start screening with no file
A skipped-sheets notice or per-sheet read-status view: none was recorded with the single-sheet test file
not_done: Getting a target figure to match did not work. 'Fig. 2'/'Fig. 3' and also 'fig2'/'fig3' all came back match_status=not_found with records_found=0, even though flags_found counted 6 and 1 flags. The manifest showed target_figures_normalized as empty strings for 'fig2'/'fig3', so the matching in this build appears broken.
Aggressive screening mode made no difference I could see on example_fabricated.csv (still 390 / 16 flags). Its effect could not be shown with this file.
Pointing Config path at a missing file ran silently with the same results and no warning, so I could not test custom thresholds.
Start screening with no file showed no message and left the previous results in place.

Cancel screening showed its notice, but the short demo run finished anyway, so I never saw a partial or cancelled result. In the replay, cancelling a Start screening run on example_fabricated.csv produced no new results, but the page then showed the heading 'Results for example_fabricated.csv' above the old synth_demo numbers and rows (150, 6 flags), so the heading names the wrong run.
The data grid's own 'Download as CSV' toolbar button produced no file in the headless browser (the DL Review Queue button did work).
The ZIP bundle was downloaded (21 KB) but is binary, so its contents could not be read here.
No Excel, PDF or ZIP input was tested; only the CSV test file was available.
The constant-ratio and repeated-error-value checks were not among the flags in either run, so the test data did not show them.
detect_constant_offsets is internally inconsistent on example_fabricated.csv: the Anomaly CSV Evidence gives an offset of 5.0 while its Chinese reason text says the difference is 0.0000.
Some output text (verdict banner, HTML report body, Anomaly CSV pattern types) is in Chinese; I recorded it as it appears.
